correctness.rationale: Correctness PASS for exactly two distinct unordered particles on the specified 16-vertex, 24-edge GP(8,3). Prue–Scrimshaw allows the 120/336/228-cell unordered cubical model (cubic graph, girth six, n=2). Fresh integer chain construction gave ∂1∂2=0, ∂2 rank208, Smith 207 units and a 2, and ∂1 rank119, hence H1=Z^9⊕Z/2 and H2=Z^20. Complete DFS gives 400 simple cycles and 111 vertex-disjoint cycle pairs: 60 of type6/6, 24 of6/8, 24 of6/10 and 3 of8/8. Every signed exterior product is a 2-cycle. The 48-element shortest-pair automorphism orbit contains an exact determinant-1 20×20 minor; saturation of ker∂2 proves an integral basis, not just rational spanning. Exact Smith factors for the remaining torus matrices give the claimed parity defects. Independent Lefschetz computation of all 96 automorphisms gives trace counts {20:1,2:16,0:66,-4:13}; mean 0. No infinite extrapolation is involved.

value.rationale: Scientific value PASS: GP(8,3) is a standard highly symmetric sparse nonplanar cubic graph. The natural shortest embedded cycle-pair classes give an integral basis already in one automorphism orbit, while the next natural cycle lengths have distinct 2-primary obstructions. These distinctions and the absence of any rational invariant H2 vector are not determined by ordinary Betti numbers, adjacency spectra or general planar graph-braid methods; a finite exact lattice benchmark is useful for understanding geometry of nonplanar graph-braid homology.
residual_risks: The result is a particular finite graph, not a uniform theorem for all generalized Petersen graphs; value rests on a canonical representative and its natural invariant, not on a claimed universal classification.

final_claim: For GP(8,3), UConf_2 has integral H_1=Z^9⊕Z/2 and H_2=Z^20. Sixty disjoint-hexagon-pair tori split under 96 graph automorphisms into orbits 12+48; the larger orbit contains an integral H_2 basis. Four length types have quotients 0, Z⊕(Z/2)^3, Z⊕(Z/2)^5, Z^17; the rational H_2 character has trace multiplicities 20:1, 2:16, 0:66, -4:13.
